# DAG Execution Engine — EPIC design (for codex review)

**Status**: DRAFT for codex adversarial review (2026-05-24). No code yet.
**Origin**: 3-way audit (me + sub-agent + codex, all verdict TRUE) found the
firmware-DAG executor (path a) is unimplemented. Audit + memory:
`project_dag_execution_engine_unimplemented`, codex audit
`docs/audit/codex-reviews/dag-execution-engine-audit-codex-2026-05-24.txt`.
**Decision to scope this** (operator, 2026-05-24): treat the firmware-DAG as a
committed capability and produce the full EPIC design + 1-3wk scope.

## 1. Problem & framing
There are TWO independent "DAG" paths in the codebase:
- **(a) DAG-plan path** — `POST /api/v1/dag` → `workflow.start(dag=…)` validates +
  persists to `dag_plans` + marks `executing`, **then stops**. No executor runs the
  tasks (compile/flash/cross-compile/package); nothing sets `completed` or calls
  `workflow.finish()` from an executor. This EPIC builds path (a).
- **(b) Orchestration path** — JIRA webhook → `orchestrator_gateway.build_catcs_from_dag`
  → `queue_backend` → `worker.py` → `run_graph` → Gerrit. **Already works**
  (the live code-authoring pipeline). NOT touched by this EPIC, but its sandbox
  runtime + queue/claim patterns are the reuse substrate.

**Goal**: a `/api/v1/dag` submission of `smoke-compile-flash-host-native` (and, in
later phases, cross-compile/package/remote-board DAGs) **executes its tasks to
`completed`**, records `workflow_steps`, and greens `staging-gate-smoke` honestly.

**Non-goals**: replacing path (b); building a new UI; multi-tenant canary (Boreas-B
Gap B, deferred). The smoke gate is NOT a live promote blocker today (canary is the
operative gate; `staging-gate-smoke.timer` is `not-found`), so this is a
capability + fidelity build, not a hotfix.

## 2. Reusable substrate (confirmed by audit — do NOT rebuild)
| Piece | File | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `dag_schema.DAG`/`Task` | backend/dag_schema.py:26 | task = `{task_id, required_tier(t1/networked/t3), toolchain, inputs, expected_output, depends_on}` |
| `dag_validator` | backend/dag_validator.py | already gates submit (cycles/MECE/tier) |
| `dag_storage` state machine | backend/dag_storage.py:54 | `executing→completed` already LEGAL; `set_status` has FOR UPDATE row-lock; lookups by id/run_id |
| `workflow.step(run, idempotency_key)` | backend/workflow.py:538 | durable append-only checkpoint; `(run_id, idempotency_key)` UNIQUE → idempotent replay; `task_id` is part of the key |
| `workflow.finish(run_id, status)` | backend/workflow.py:340 | terminal run transition |
| `container.dispatch_t3 / start_container / exec_in_container` | backend/container.py:930/585/986 | sandbox exec primitives |
| `t3_resolver.resolve_t3_runner` | backend/t3_resolver.py:109 | LOCAL vs BUNDLE/SSH decision (host_native → LOCAL) |
| `ssh_runner.run_on_target` | backend/ssh_runner.py | real remote-board exec (t3 BUNDLE) |
| `sandbox_prewarm` | backend/sandbox_prewarm.py | topo-orders + pre-warms in-degree-0 tasks (reuse the topo walk) |
| `SandboxRuntime` protocol (`LocalSandboxRuntime`) | backend/worker.py:205 | prepare/run sandbox; path-b's executor substrate |

## 3. Target architecture
A **DAG executor** that turns an `executing` plan into a completed run:

```
[plan claimer] → [topo scheduler] → [task dispatch] → [handler] → [step record] → [terminal wiring]
  poll/claim       ready set          by toolchain     compile/    workflow.step    set_status(completed)
  executing        honor depends_on   + required_tier  flash/...   (idempotent)     + workflow.finish
```

### Components (each ≈ a child Story)
- **E1 — Plan claimer / executor loop.** Poll `dag_plans WHERE status='executing'`,
  claim with a lease so multi-replica backends/workers don't double-run. Reuse the
  OP-977 fencing-token pattern (`claim:{instance}:{epoch}-{uuid}`, lowest-token-wins)
  or `SELECT … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`. Lease renew + reclaim on crash.
- **E2 — Topological scheduler.** Build the ready-set from `depends_on` (reuse
  `sandbox_prewarm`'s indegree walk), run ready tasks (bounded concurrency within a
  plan), advance as deps complete. Fail-fast vs continue-on-error policy.
- **E3 — Task-type → handler dispatch.** Registry keyed on `toolchain` × `required_tier`.
  t1 = local sandbox container; networked = sandbox + egress; t3 = `t3_resolver` →
  LOCAL (host-native, same arch/OS) or BUNDLE/SSH (`ssh_runner`). **CLAUDE.md rule:
  cross-compile MUST use the platform toolchain from `get_platform_config` +
  `-DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE` + `--sysroot` — never system gcc.**
- **E4 — Task handlers.** `compile` (cmake/make/host gcc; cross via platform
  toolchain), `flash` (host_native LOCAL = symbolic/no-op-to-loopback; real device =
  `ssh_runner`/hardware bridge), `package`, `cross-compile`. Each runs the task's
  `toolchain` command in a workspace, captures rc/stdout/artifact at `expected_output`.
- **E5 — Step recording + artifact check.** One `workflow.step` per task (idempotency
  key includes `task_id`); validate `expected_output` produced; link
  `workflow_steps.dag_task_id`.
- **E6 — Terminal wiring.** All tasks ok → `set_status(plan,'completed')` +
  `workflow.finish(run,'completed')`. Any fail → `failed` + finish `failed`/`halted`
  (+ optional Phase 56-DAG-C mutation hook).
- **E7 — Failure / retry / crash-resume.** Idempotent re-claim skips done steps (via
  `workflow.step` UNIQUE); per-task retry policy; poison-plan handling.
- **E8 — Side-effect isolation.** Dev/staging MUST NOT touch prod artifacts/registry/
  Gerrit/real hardware. Env-gated handler "test mode" (symbolic flash, scratch
  workspace, no push). Ties to A2 env-contract.
- **E9 — Deployment.** Decide: in-process lifespan task gated by
  `OMNISIGHT_DAG_EXECUTOR_ENABLED` vs a separate worker container/systemd unit
  (mirror `omnisight-worker@`). Wire onto staging; re-green `staging-gate-smoke`;
  re-enable the timer. 4-AC + Go-Live.
- **E10 — Observability + honesty pass.** Executor heartbeat/metrics; fix misleading
  surfaces (`TODO.md:131` "2 real DAGs end-to-end"; any `/api/v1/dag`-as-executable
  product copy).

## 4. Phasing & effort (3-way consensus)
- **Phase 1 — Smoke MVP (~2-5 person-days, MEDIUM risk).** E1(single-claim) + E2 +
  E3/E4 for host-native `compile`+`flash` only (LocalSandboxRuntime, symbolic flash)
  + E5 + E6 happy-path + E8 test-mode. Outcome: `smoke-compile-flash-host-native`
  reaches `completed`; smoke gate greens for real on staging.
- **Phase 2 — Tier expansion (~1 week).** cross-compile (platform toolchain rule) +
  package + t3 BUNDLE/SSH remote-board via `ssh_runner`; the second smoke DAG
  (`smoke-cross-compile-aarch64`).
- **Phase 3 — Production hardening (~1 week).** Multi-replica claim/fencing (E1 full),
  retry/crash-resume (E7), failure semantics, full side-effect isolation, metrics.
- **Total: ~1-3 weeks** depending on how far past MVP.

## 5. Open questions for codex
1. **In-process vs separate worker (E9).** A lifespan background task in the staging
   backend is simplest but couples executor lifecycle to the API process + multiplies
   across replicas (a/b) → needs claim even for MVP. A separate worker
   (mirror `omnisight-worker@`) is cleaner isolation but more infra. Which for MVP?
2. **Should path (a) and path (b) converge?** Both use `dag_schema.DAG` + a sandbox
   runtime. Is building a *second* executor the right call, or should path-a DAGs be
   lowered into path-b TaskCards (reuse `worker.py` + queue) so there's ONE execution
   substrate? Trade-off: reuse vs the two having different semantics (dag_plans
   lifecycle + workflow_steps vs CATC queue + Gerrit push).
3. **What does host-native `flash` even mean (E4)?** On a server there's no device.
   Is symbolic/no-op flash an honest "completed", or does that make the smoke gate
   test a hollow path? Should the smoke DAG be redefined to something with real
   host-native semantics (compile + run-tests) instead of compile+flash?
4. **Claim mechanism for MVP (E1).** `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` (DB-native, simple) vs
   the OP-977 fencing-token pattern (already in-codebase for runners). Given staging
   has backend-a + backend-b, even MVP needs *some* claim — which?
5. **Side-effect isolation (E8).** Is an env flag (`OMNISIGHT_DAG_EXECUTOR_TEST_MODE`)
   enough, or must handlers hard-refuse prod artifact/registry/Gerrit endpoints when
   `OMNISIGHT_ENV != prod` (defense-in-depth like the A2 contract)?
6. **Is this worth building at all** given the runner-as-product pivot — i.e. is the
   firmware compile/flash capability still strategically wanted, or should Phase 1
   stop at "smoke greens" and the rest stay parked? (Operator already chose to scope
   it; codex: sanity-check whether the EPIC over-builds vs the actual product need.)
7. **MECE / artifact collisions** on a shared staging workspace across concurrent
   plans (E2/E8) — does `expected_output` + `output_overlap_ack` suffice, or is
   per-plan workspace isolation required from day 1?

---

## 6. codex review round 1 (2026-05-24) — folded in
**Verdict: SOUND-WITH-CHANGES.** Audit: `docs/audit/codex-reviews/dag-engine-epic-design-codex-2026-05-24.txt`. Corrections, all to apply before/within implementation:

### Three data-model blockers (must fix first — were not in the original draft)
- **B1 — `executing → failed` is currently ILLEGAL.** The `dag_storage` state machine
  only allows `executing → {completed, mutated, exhausted}` (dag_storage.py:54-58). E6
  must first ADD an `executing → failed` transition (matches `workflow.finish(...,"failed")`).
- **B2 — step attribution gap.** `workflow_steps.dag_task_id` column exists (db.py:271)
  but `_record_step()` doesn't write it (workflow.py:512). E5 must extend `workflow.step()`
  to persist `dag_task_id` — "link dag_task_id" is NOT achievable as-is.
- **B3 — claim columns don't exist.** MVP needs `claim_owner/claim_token/claim_expires_at/
  heartbeat_at` on `dag_plans` (or a `dag_plan_claims` table) with compare-and-set. The
  existing runner-claim code (runner_coordination.py) is sync-SQLite + shadow-era — copy
  the *pattern*, not the module.

### Answers to the 7 open questions (resolved)
1. **Separate `omnisight-dag-executor` process/systemd unit, NOT FastAPI lifespan** — a
   lifespan task multiplies across backend-a/b on staging; a separate process gives clean
   lifecycle/restart/logs/kill-switch. (E9 decided.)
2. **Do NOT converge path-a into path-b.** `build_catcs_from_dag` + `worker.py` always run
   agent work + commit + push to Gerrit (orchestrator_gateway.py:370, worker.py:1006-1052);
   it does not aggregate deps, record `workflow_steps`, or call `finish()`. Lifecycles are
   incompatible. Build a path-a executor; reuse only LOW-level primitives (LocalSandboxRuntime
   workspace isolation, queue/lease patterns) — never `Worker.handle()` as-is.
3. **Symbolic host-native `flash` is a HOLLOW green** — docs/operations/sandbox.md:320,325
   explicitly: "You can't pretend to flash a board over localhost." **Redefine smoke DAG1 to
   `compile → run-artifact-check` / `compile → run-self-test`** (step 2 actually consumes
   `build/firmware.bin`, writes `logs/test.log`). This is the honest-slice fix. (E4/E10.)
4. **MVP REQUIRES a claim** — `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` alone is insufficient unless the row
   is leased-before-commit; use compare-and-set lease w/ expiry (B3). backend-a+b → real
   double-execution risk without it.
5. **Env flag alone insufficient** — hard fail-closed points (modelled on the A2
   `backend/env_contract.py` guard, :136/190/200) for Gerrit push, registry publish, SSH/
   remote exec, hardware flash, prod-DB writes, host mutation: refuse real side effects
   unless `OMNISIGHT_ENV=prod` AND explicit per-capability allow flags. (E8 hardened.)
6. **Phase 1 worth building** (current smoke claims are misleading). **Phase 2/3 over-build
   for the runner-as-product pivot — PARK real board flashing, SSH remote-board execution,
   package registry, and cross-compile breadth** until a real product user needs them.
7. **`expected_output`/`output_overlap_ack` NOT enough** (schema only validates *declared*
   outputs; real tools write elsewhere) — **per-plan/per-task workspace isolation from day 1**
   (LocalSandboxRuntime already creates fresh workspaces, worker.py:280-304). (E2/E8.)

### Corrected Phase-1 "smallest honest slice"
Separate `dag_executor` process · DB lease claim w/ expiry · **serial** topo execution first
(concurrency deferred) · handlers for `cmake`/`make`/`python3` only, in isolated scratch
workspaces · smoke DAG = `compile → verify/run-test` (NOT symbolic flash) · one `workflow.step`
per task with `dag_task_id` · terminal wiring `dag_plans.completed/failed` + `workflow.finish()`
· side effects fail-closed outside prod. This proves submit→claim→dep-order→sandbox-exec→
artifact→step-record→terminal — a *real* green.

### Corrected effort (codex; my 2-5d MVP was optimistic)
- **Honest MVP: 4-7 person-days**, medium risk (the +days = claim schema B3 + step-attr B2 +
  state-machine B1 + honest-smoke redesign).
- **Full cross-compile/package/SSH path: 2-4 weeks**, medium-high risk.
- **Real hardware flash: PARKED** unless a current product requirement exists.

operative gate; `staging-gate-smoke.timer` is `not-found`), so this is a
capability + fidelity build, not a hotfix.

## 3. Target architecture
A **DAG executor** that turns an `executing` plan into a completed run:

```
[plan claimer] → [topo scheduler] → [task dispatch] → [handler] → [step record] → [terminal wiring]
  poll/claim       ready set          by toolchain     compile/    workflow.step    set_status(completed)
  executing        honor depends_on   + required_tier  flash/...   (idempotent)     + workflow.finish
```

### Components (each ≈ a child Story)
- **E1 — Plan claimer / executor loop.** Poll `dag_plans WHERE status='executing'`,
  claim with a lease so multi-replica backends/workers don't double-run. Reuse the
  OP-977 fencing-token pattern (`claim:{instance}:{epoch}-{uuid}`, lowest-token-wins)
  or `SELECT … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`. Lease renew + reclaim on crash.
- **E2 — Topological scheduler.** Build the ready-set from `depends_on` (reuse
  `sandbox_prewarm`'s indegree walk), run ready tasks (bounded concurrency within a
  plan), advance as deps complete. Fail-fast vs continue-on-error policy.
- **E3 — Task-type → handler dispatch.** Registry keyed on `toolchain` × `required_tier`.
  t1 = local sandbox container; networked = sandbox + egress; t3 = `t3_resolver` →
  LOCAL (host-native, same arch/OS) or BUNDLE/SSH (`ssh_runner`). **CLAUDE.md rule:
  cross-compile MUST use the platform toolchain from `get_platform_config` +
  `-DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE` + `--sysroot` — never system gcc.**
- **E4 — Task handlers.** `compile` (cmake/make/host gcc; cross via platform
  toolchain), `flash` (host_native LOCAL = symbolic/no-op-to-loopback; real device =
  `ssh_runner`/hardware bridge), `package`, `cross-compile`. Each runs the task's
  `toolchain` command in a workspace, captures rc/stdout/artifact at `expected_output`.
- **E5 — Step recording + artifact check.** One `workflow.step` per task (idempotency
  key includes `task_id`); validate `expected_output` produced; link
  `workflow_steps.dag_task_id`.
- **E6 — Terminal wiring.** All tasks ok → `set_status(plan,'completed')` +
  `workflow.finish(run,'completed')`. Any fail → `failed` + finish `failed`/`halted`
  (+ optional Phase 56-DAG-C mutation hook).
- **E7 — Failure / retry / crash-resume.** Idempotent re-claim skips done steps (via
  `workflow.step` UNIQUE); per-task retry policy; poison-plan handling.
- **E8 — Side-effect isolation.** Dev/staging MUST NOT touch prod artifacts/registry/
  Gerrit/real hardware. Env-gated handler "test mode" (symbolic flash, scratch
  workspace, no push). Ties to A2 env-contract.
- **E9 — Deployment.** Decide: in-process lifespan task gated by
  `OMNISIGHT_DAG_EXECUTOR_ENABLED` vs a separate worker container/systemd unit
  (mirror `omnisight-worker@`). Wire onto staging; re-green `staging-gate-smoke`;
  re-enable the timer. 4-AC + Go-Live.
- **E10 — Observability + honesty pass.** Executor heartbeat/metrics; fix misleading
  surfaces (`TODO.md:131` "2 real DAGs end-to-end"; any `/api/v1/dag`-as-executable
  product copy).

## 4. Phasing & effort (3-way consensus)
- **Phase 1 — Smoke MVP (~2-5 person-days, MEDIUM risk).** E1(single-claim) + E2 +
  E3/E4 for host-native `compile`+`flash` only (LocalSandboxRuntime, symbolic flash)
  + E5 + E6 happy-path + E8 test-mode. Outcome: `smoke-compile-flash-host-native`
  reaches `completed`; smoke gate greens for real on staging.
- **Phase 2 — Tier expansion (~1 week).** cross-compile (platform toolchain rule) +
  package + t3 BUNDLE/SSH remote-board via `ssh_runner`; the second smoke DAG
  (`smoke-cross-compile-aarch64`).
- **Phase 3 — Production hardening (~1 week).** Multi-replica claim/fencing (E1 full),
  retry/crash-resume (E7), failure semantics, full side-effect isolation, metrics.
- **Total: ~1-3 weeks** depending on how far past MVP.

## 5. Open questions for codex
1. **In-process vs separate worker (E9).** A lifespan background task in the staging
   backend is simplest but couples executor lifecycle to the API process + multiplies
   across replicas (a/b) → needs claim even for MVP. A separate worker
   (mirror `omnisight-worker@`) is cleaner isolation but more infra. Which for MVP?
2. **Should path (a) and path (b) converge?** Both use `dag_schema.DAG` + a sandbox
   runtime. Is building a *second* executor the right call, or should path-a DAGs be
   lowered into path-b TaskCards (reuse `worker.py` + queue) so there's ONE execution
   substrate? Trade-off: reuse vs the two having different semantics (dag_plans
   lifecycle + workflow_steps vs CATC queue + Gerrit push).
3. **What does host-native `flash` even mean (E4)?** On a server there's no device.
   Is symbolic/no-op flash an honest "completed", or does that make the smoke gate
   test a hollow path? Should the smoke DAG be redefined to something with real
   host-native semantics (compile + run-tests) instead of compile+flash?
4. **Claim mechanism for MVP (E1).** `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` (DB-native, simple) vs
   the OP-977 fencing-token pattern (already in-codebase for runners). Given staging
   has backend-a + backend-b, even MVP needs *some* claim — which?
5. **Side-effect isolation (E8).** Is an env flag (`OMNISIGHT_DAG_EXECUTOR_TEST_MODE`)
   enough, or must handlers hard-refuse prod artifact/registry/Gerrit endpoints when
   `OMNISIGHT_ENV != prod` (defense-in-depth like the A2 contract)?
6. **Is this worth building at all** given the runner-as-product pivot — i.e. is the
   firmware compile/flash capability still strategically wanted, or should Phase 1
   stop at "smoke greens" and the rest stay parked? (Operator already chose to scope
   it; codex: sanity-check whether the EPIC over-builds vs the actual product need.)
7. **MECE / artifact collisions** on a shared staging workspace across concurrent
   plans (E2/E8) — does `expected_output` + `output_overlap_ack` suffice, or is
   per-plan workspace isolation required from day 1?

     2	
     3	Pydantic models that mirror the Orchestrator template's JSON contract

    41	    # benchmark runs writing the same report path that's later merged).
    42	    output_overlap_ack: bool = False
    43

    45	    @classmethod
    46	    def _id_is_simple(cls, v: str) -> str:
    47	        # Keep id printable — used as Decision Engine key + as part of
    48	        # workflow_steps.idempotency_key (Phase 56-DAG-B).
    49	        if not v.replace("-", "").replace("_", "").isalnum():
    50	            raise ValueError(
    51	                "task_id must be alphanumeric / dash / underscore only"
    52	            )
    53	        return v
    54	
    55	    @field_validator("depends_on")
    56	    @classmethod
    57	    def _no_self_dep(cls, v: list[str], info) -> list[str]:
    58	        tid = info.data.get("task_id")
    59	        if tid and tid in v:
    60	            raise ValueError(f"task {tid!r} cannot depend on itself")
    61	        if len(v) != len(set(v)):
    62	            raise ValueError("depends_on must not contain duplicates")
    63	        return v

    67	    """The full planning artefact."""

docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:14:**Amends**: ADR-0017 (Release conductor), ADR-0018 (Event-driven release pipeline), ADR-0019 (`release:force-promote` override), ADR-0021 (Release Pipeline Coordinator).
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:34:3. **A release = a promoted IMAGE tag + digest recorded in `release_train`** (NOT a `v*` git tag — see Decision RT-20 below; a git tag would trigger the existing CI `^v` build rule and rebuild a different digest, breaking "validated digest == shipped digest"). Candidate images are built from a chosen develop SHA via pipeline-API (`CANDIDATE_SHA`); promotion retags the validated digest to `vX.Y.Z` in GitLab CR.
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:36:5. **Promotion is by image digest**, not rebuild: the tagged image rides staging → canary (prod backend-a) → prod (backend-b).
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:57:2. **"Every tag prod-usable" has no test gate.** `.gitlab-ci.yml` has no test/lint stage; Gerrit `Verified` is disabled (`applicableIf=is:false`). A `v*` tag can build+sign+attest without ever proving the suite passed at that SHA — and a bad tag is a *permanent* release object. Auto-cut needs a real per-SHA green signal (pytest + FE build/typecheck + migration check + smoke/canary) before it may tag.
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:62:7. **Registry/`latest` "green-but-not-deployed" risk.** Staging compose still defaults GHCR `:latest`; prod compose defaults `OMNISIGHT_IMAGE_TAG=latest`. Unset tag → deploys newest regardless of approval. Make staging+prod **fail closed** on unset tag; share one registry/tag/digest contract across CI/staging/prod/health. Also: expose `git_ref`/`git_sha` in `/api/version`; make `frontend_compat` an actual gate or stop documenting it as one.
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:68:3. **Convert deploy validation atomically**: `deploy-prod.sh` + `scripts/check_deploy_ref.sh` + `deploy/prod-deploy-allowlist.txt` + runbook — tag/digest-only, refuse branch refs.
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:72:7. **Update conductor/coordinator** to key release identity on immutable tag/SHA/digest, not main promotion.
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:77:**Rollback**: pre-cut → re-enable old units/allowlist only if no v* tag was cut under the new model. Post-cut → never delete/move immutable tags; roll back by deploying the previous approved `v*` tag/digest (subject to migration compat); mark a bad cut in audit metadata rather than retagging.
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:82:- Staging + prod pull the same registry namespace + immutable tag/digest scheme; unset tag fails closed.
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:85:- Supply-chain audit truthfully reflects actual signing mode + final image digests.
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:89:- **Candidate-artifact model = revised Model A** (`docs/design/2026-05-21-model-a-candidate-build-release-train.md`): build `sha-<fullsha>` from a chosen green develop SHA via pipeline-API; validate on staging by digest; promote = retag the SAME digest to the reserved `vX.Y.Z`. Resolves BLOCKING hole #1.
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:90:- **RT-20 (final release identity) = IMAGE-TAG-ONLY.** No `v*` git tag is created (avoids the CI-rebuild hazard with zero fragility — no need to special-case the CI workflow rule). Release identity = promoted GitLab CR image tag `vX.Y.Z` (→ validated digest) + `release_train`/`release_audit` row. Git/human provenance = the audit row (git_sha + digests); optionally a NON-`v*`-matching ref like `released/vX.Y.Z` created post-promote (CI never fires on it). Rationale: prod already runs pinned images not git refs; main is retired; the audit row is the authoritative record; avoids fragile CI tag-exclusion logic.
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:91:- **RT-21 (bridge) = release-train tracks BACKEND + FRONTEND digests only (a PAIR, not a triplet).** Verified this session: prod compose deploys backend-a/b + frontend (no bridge container); the gerrit-jira-bridge/coordinator run as host daemons from the `sora-bridge` develop checkout (control-plane, separate concern). The `bridge` image build is decoupled from the release-train promote/deploy gate. (If bridge is ever containerised into prod, add it then.)
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:92:- **RT-08-pre (overlay load semantics) = READ-BEFORE-START from an env lock.** The deploy/promote step writes a digest+identity lock; the container reads it once at startup; `/api/version` serves it. Rationale: deploys always rolling-restart anyway, so "needs restart to update" is not a limitation; deterministic; no per-request IO or cache-invalidation failure modes; fail-closed (missing lock at startup → readiness fails → deploy gate catches it).

docs/sop/lessons/L-OP-977-idempotent-label-add-is-not-a-mutex.md:2:id: L-OP-977
docs/sop/lessons/L-OP-977-idempotent-label-add-is-not-a-mutex.md:3:ticket: OP-977
docs/sop/lessons/L-OP-977-idempotent-label-add-is-not-a-mutex.md:15:**Fix (OP-977 / AUDIT-24)**: replace the bare label with a **fencing token** — `claim:{instance_id}:{epoch_us:016d}-{uuid8}`, unique per attempt — and decide the winner by `min(...)` over *all* `claim:{instance_id}:*` labels in the post-PUT readback. The winner is now a function of a **total order over a set every racer observes identically**, not of "did my idempotent write succeed". The loser leaves its label for GC so the winner re-evaluating `min(...)` never flips. Stale tokens (crashed runners) are swept once aged past `2× CLI timeout`; pre-AUDIT-24 bare labels are treated as expired. Rollback flag `OMNISIGHT_RUNNER_ATOMIC_CLAIM_LEGACY=1`. Race-simulation suite `backend/tests/test_atomic_claim_race.py` reproduces the OP-974 schedule (two threads, same `instance_id`, same bot, fully interleaved GET/PUT/GET) and asserts exactly one wins and the lowest token wins for every token assignment. Pattern doc: `docs/sop/runner-pickup-mutex.md`.

docs/audit/codex-reviews/dag-engine-epic-design-codex-2026-05-24.txt:10694:docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:57:2. **"Every tag prod-usable" has no test gate.** `.gitlab-ci.yml` has no test/lint stage; Gerrit `Verified` is disabled (`applicableIf=is:false`). A `v*` tag can build+sign+attest without ever proving the suite passed at that SHA — and a bad tag is a *permanent* release object. Auto-cut needs a real per-SHA green signal (pytest + FE build/typecheck + migration check + smoke/canary) before it may tag.

docs/audit/codex-reviews/dag-engine-epic-design-codex-2026-05-24.txt:10706:docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:90:- **RT-20 (final release identity) = IMAGE-TAG-ONLY.** No `v*` git tag is created (avoids the CI-rebuild hazard with zero fragility — no need to special-case the CI workflow rule). Release identity = promoted GitLab CR image tag `vX.Y.Z` (→ validated digest) + `release_train`/`release_audit` row. Git/human provenance = the audit row (git_sha + digests); optionally a NON-`v*`-matching ref like `released/vX.Y.Z` created post-promote (CI never fires on it). Rationale: prod already runs pinned images not git refs; main is retired; the audit row is the authoritative record; avoids fragile CI tag-exclusion logic.

docs/audit/codex-reviews/coldstart-acting-blast-radius-codex-audit-2026-05-23.txt:2580:/home/user/sora-bridge/docs/sop/lessons/L-OP-977-idempotent-label-add-is-not-a-mutex.md:15:**Fix (OP-977 / AUDIT-24)**: replace the bare label with a **fencing token** — `claim:{instance_id}:{epoch_us:016d}-{uuid8}`, unique per attempt — and decide the winner by `min(...)` over *all* `claim:{instance_id}:*` labels in the post-PUT readback. The winner is now a function of a **total order over a set every racer observes identically**, not of "did my idempotent write succeed". The loser leaves its label for GC so the winner re-evaluating `min(...)` never flips. Stale tokens (crashed runners) are swept once aged past `2× CLI timeout`; pre-AUDIT-24 bare labels are treated as expired. Rollback flag `OMNISIGHT_RUNNER_ATOMIC_CLAIM_LEGACY=1`. Race-simulation suite `backend/tests/test_atomic_claim_race.py` reproduces the OP-974 schedule (two threads, same `instance_id`, same bot, fully interleaved GET/PUT/GET) and asserts exactly one wins and the lowest token wins for every token assignment. Pattern doc: `docs/sop/runner-pickup-mutex.md`.

docs/audit/codex-reviews/model-b-rc-promote-codex-audit-2026-05-21.txt:1:# Codex audit — Model B rc-tag -> promote-by-digest release train
docs/audit/codex-reviews/model-b-rc-promote-codex-audit-2026-05-21.txt:5:## A. Promote-by-digest correctness
docs/audit/codex-reviews/model-b-rc-promote-codex-audit-2026-05-21.txt:8:- Evidence: ADR-0040 says “A release = a `v*` git tag on a develop commit” and that the tag triggers GitLab CI build/sign/SBOM/attest/bundle (docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:34). The GitLab workflow runs for any `$CI_COMMIT_TAG =~ /^v.*/` (.gitlab-ci.yml:1-4). Model B says promotion re-tags digest D to `:v0.6.0` with no rebuild (docs/design/2026-05-21-model-b-rc-promote-release-train.md:26-28).
docs/audit/codex-reviews/model-b-rc-promote-codex-audit-2026-05-21.txt:11:- Fix: Decide one model. Either (1) final git tags are metadata only and GitLab workflow must explicitly not rebuild final tags, routing them to a promote-by-digest job with a recorded rc source digest; or (2) no final git tag exists and ADR-0040 must be revised to say release identity is image digest plus promoted image tag, not git tag.
docs/audit/codex-reviews/model-b-rc-promote-codex-audit-2026-05-21.txt:13:A2. HIGH — Current pipeline signs and attests by digest, but the verification/audit story is inconsistent and no final-target verification exists.
docs/audit/codex-reviews/model-b-rc-promote-codex-audit-2026-05-21.txt:14:- Evidence: `sign-image` resolves the digest from the sha tag and signs `${IMAGE_BASE}@${DIGEST}` with `cosign sign --key "$COSIGN_KEY"` (.gitlab-ci.yml:143-151). `attest-image` also attests `${IMAGE_BASE}@${DIGEST}` with `--key "$COSIGN_KEY"` (.gitlab-ci.yml:179-200). But audit JSON claims `signed_with: "cosign-keyless-gitlab-oidc"` (.gitlab-ci.yml:259-287), and `scripts/verify_image_signature.sh` falls back to GitHub Actions keyless identity if no PEM key is found (scripts/verify_image_signature.sh:16-24, scripts/verify_image_signature.sh:108-118).
docs/audit/codex-reviews/model-b-rc-promote-codex-audit-2026-05-21.txt:15:- Flaw: Digest signing itself survives a retag, but the declared verifier mode does not match the signer mode. A final promote can pass “signed by digest” in principle while every downstream verifier expecting keyless GitHub/GitLab OIDC fails.
docs/audit/codex-reviews/model-b-rc-promote-codex-audit-2026-05-21.txt:17:- Fix: Pick one trust mode. table-level、alembic-vs-live column-level 是第三軸從沒守住。(d) **Sub-phase 3-C 第二次 crash — `event_log.id` 沒 IDENTITY**：`int(None)` on `reset_identity_sequences`；root cause：0001 baseline 寫 `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` 沒 AUTOINCREMENT、`alembic_pg_compat._translate_autoincrement` 的 regex 只抓顯式 AUTOINCREMENT、PG 拿 plain int；app 的 `INSERT INTO event_log (event_type, ...)` 會 NOT NULL violation。(e) **Sub-phase 3-C 第三次 DEFAULT AS IDENTITY`（讀 `pg_attribute.attidentity` 判斷避免 double-ADD）；`alembic_pg_compat._translate_real` 加 `REAL → DOUBLE PRECISION`，DDL-only 預防（`_DDL_GUARD_RE` filter `CREATE TABLE`/`ALTER TABLE`/`ADD COLUMN` 避免參數字串誤傷）；`backend/tests/test_migrator_schema_coverage.py::test_alembic_pg_matches_sqlite_column_by_column` 跨 dialect column-parity 測試（`OMNI_TEST_PG_URL` env skip pattern、CI    573	_CAPABILITY_MATRIX: capability_matrix.CapabilityMatrix | None = None
   574	
   575	# Side channel for `_build_prompt` → `main()`: stash the resolved capability
   576	# set under the ticket key so main() can gate sensitive ops (gerrit push,
   577	# jira update, ...) without re-fetching the issue. Cleared once main() has
   578	# consumed the value; the slot tolerates back-to-back pickups in the same
   579	# process because each tick overwrites the previous entry.
   580	_LAST_RESOLVED_CAPABILITIES: dict[str, frozenset[str]] = {}
   581	_LAST_TICKET_METADATA: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}
   582	_LAST_AGENT_FEATURE_FLAGS: dict[str, dict[str, bool]] = {}
   583	
   584	
   585	def _load_capability_matrix() -> capability_matrix.CapabilityMatrix:
   586	    """Lazy-load + cache ``config/capability_matrix.yaml`` for this process."""
   587	    global _CAPABILITY_MATRIX
   588	    if _CAPABILITY_MATRIX is None:
   589	        _CAPABILITY_MATRIX = capability_matrix.load_capability_matrix()
   590	    return _CAPABILITY_MATRIX

   593	def _resolve_runner_capabilities(
   594	    ticket_type: str,
   595	    declared_areas: list[str],
   596	    tier: str,
   597	    labels: list[str],
   598	) -> frozenset[str]:
   599	    """Resolve runner capabilities for the current ticket (AC#3 + AC#4).
   600	
   601	    Multi-area tickets union the per-area capability sets; the operator
   602	    label overrides (``capability:enable=`` / ``capability:disable=``)
   603	    apply on top so a problematic capability can be removed without
   604	    touching the YAML.
   605	    """
   606	    matrix = _load_capability_matrix()
   607	    if declared_areas:
   608	        return matrix.resolve_for_areas(
   609	            ticket_type, declared_areas, tier, labels=labels,
   610	        )
   611	    return matrix.resolve(ticket_type, "<no-area>", tier, labels=labels)

   614	def _pre_pickup_cap_gate_enabled() -> bool:
   615	    return os.environ.get(PRE_PICKUP_CAP_GATE_ENV, "on").strip().lower() not in {
   616	        "0", "false", "no", "off",
   617	    }

   619	
   620	def _required_capabilities_for(snapshot: scheduler.TicketSnapshot) -> frozenset[str]:
   621	    """Infer the minimum runner capabilities needed before CLI pickup."""
   622	    labels = {label.strip().lower() for label in getattr(snapshot, "labels", ())}
   623	    required = {"jira_update"}
   624	    if labels & {"type:feature", "type:bug", "type:docs"}:
   625	        required.add("code_edit")
   626	    if "type:meta" not in labels and "runner:no-commits-expected" not in labels:
   627	        required.add("gerrit_push")
   628	    return frozenset(required)
   629	
   630	
   631	def _capability_context_for_snapshot(
   632	    client: jira_dispatch.DispatchClient,
   633	    snapshot: scheduler.TicketSnapshot,
   634	) -> tuple[str, list[str], str, list[str]]:
   635	    issue = jira_dispatch._request(
   636	        client, "GET", f"/issue/{snapshot.key}?fields=labels,issuetype",
   637	    )
   638	    fields = issue.get("fields") or {}
   639	    labels = list(fields.get("labels") or getattr(snapshot, "labels", ()))
   640	    issuetype_raw = fields.get("issuetype") or {}
   641	    ticket_type = (
   642	        issuetype_raw.get("name", "Story")
   643	        if isinstance(issuetype_raw, dict)
   644	        else "Story"
   645	    )
   646	    declared_areas = sorted(
   647	        label.split(":", 1)[1] for label in labels if label.startswith("area:")
   648	    )
   649	    tier = next(
   650	        (label.split(":", 1)[1] for label in labels if label.startswith("tier:")),
   651	        "M",
   652	    )
   653	    return ticket_type, declared_areas, tier, labels
   654	
   655	
   656	def _increment_pre_pickup_cap_gate_metric(
   657	    areas: list[str],
   658	    tier: str,
   659	    issuetype: str,
   660	) -> None:
   661	    try:
   662	        from backend import metrics as _metrics
   663	
   664	        for area in areas or ["<no-area>"]:
   665	            _metrics.runner_pre_pickup_cap_gate_blocked_total.labels(
   666	                area=area, tier=tier, issuetype=issuetype,
   667	            ).inc()
   668	    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - observability must not block pickup
   669	        log.debug("pre-pickup capability gate metric publish failed", exc_info=True)
   670	
   671	
   672	def _pre_pickup_capability_ok(
   673	    client: jira_dispatch.DispatchClient,
   674	    snapshot: scheduler.TicketSnapshot,
   675	    matrix: capability_matrix.CapabilityMatrix,
   676	) -> tuple[bool, str | None]:
   677	    """Return whether matrix capabilities satisfy pre-CLI required caps."""
   678	    if not _pre_pickup_cap_gate_enabled():
   679	        return True, None
   680	    ticket_type, declared_areas, tier, labels = _capability_context_for_snapshot(
   681	        client, snapshot,
   682	    )
   683	    if declared_areas:
   684	        resolved = matrix.resolve_for_areas(
   685	            ticket_type, declared_areas, tier, labels=labels, ticket_id=snapshot.key,
   686	        )
   687	    else:
   688	        resolved = matrix.resolve(
   689	            ticket_type, "<no-area>", tier, labels=labels, ticket_id=snapshot.key,
   690	        )
   691	    required = _required_capabilities_for(snapshot)
   692	    if required <= resolved:
   693	        return True, None
   694	    _increment_pre_pickup_cap_gate_metric(declared_areas, tier, ticket_type)
   695	    need = ",".join(sorted(required - resolved))
   696	    have = ",".join(sorted(resolved)) or "(none)"
   697	    return False, f"capability-mismatch: need={need} have={have}"
   698

   700	def _post_pre_pickup_capability_block(
   701	    client: jira_dispatch.DispatchClient,
   702	    snapshot: scheduler.TicketSnapshot,

   705	    print(f"[runner] pre-pickup capability blocked {snapshot.key}: {reason}")

   707	        return

   709	        client,
   710	        snapshot.key,

   714	            "Pre-pickup capability gate failed; CLI was not invoked.\n\n"
   715	            f"{reason}\n\n"
   716	            "Operator: extend `config/capability_matrix.yaml` for this "
   717	            "ticket type / area / tier, or use `capability:enable=` for a "
   718	            "one-shot override."
   719	        ),
   720	    )

   723	def _require_runner_capability(
   724	    client: jira_dispatch.DispatchClient,
   725	    snapshot: scheduler.TicketSnapshot,
   726	    enabled: frozenset[str],
   727	    capability: str,
   728	    claim: "jira_dispatch.ClaimResult | None" = None,
   729	) -> bool:
   730	    """Enforce a capability before the runner performs a sensitive op.
   731	
   732	    OP-1524: when ``claim`` is supplied (the post-pickup ``gerrit_push``
   733	    gate at line ~2700), the runner's own ``claim:{INSTANCE_ID}:*`` label
   734	    is stripped BEFORE the revert comment + transition fire, so the next
   735	    pickup is not blocked by a stale claim from this aborted run.
   736	    """

   738	        capability_matrix.require_capability(enabled, capability)
   739	        return True
   740	    except capability_matrix.CapabilityNotPermitted as e:
   741	        print(

   743	            f"enabled={sorted(enabled)}",
   744	            file=sys.stderr,
   745	        )
   746	        if not DRY_RUN:
   747	            _release_ticket_claim_if_acquired(client, snapshot.key, claim)

   751	                f"Operator: extend `config/capability_matrix.yaml` for this "
   752	                f"(ticket_type × area × tier) combination, or add label "
   753	                f"`capability:enable={capability}` to grant a one-shot override.",
   754	            )
   755	            try:
   756	                jira_dispatch.transition_back_to_todo(
   757	                    client, snapshot.key,
   758	                    f"[runner-capability-blocked] {capability!r} not permitted",
   759	                )
   760	            except Exception as revert_err:  # noqa: BLE001 — log + continue
  1480	            print(f"[runner] could not even post skip comment: {inner}", file=sys.stderr)
  1481	        return
  1482	
  1483	    if transitioned:
  1484	        print(f"[runner] {key} → Under Review. Reviewer: +2 in Gerrit UI.")
  1485	    else:

  1487	              f"comment posted, transition skipped")

  1490	def _claim_token_suffix(
  1491	    claim: "jira_dispatch.ClaimResult | None",
  1492	) -> str | None:
  1493	    """Bare fencing token from a won ``ClaimResult``.
  1494	
  1495	    ``ClaimResult.claim_token`` is ``{INSTANCE_ID}:{token}``; this strips the
  1496	    ``{INSTANCE_ID}:`` prefix to yield the bare token used to build the fenced
  1497	    label ``claim:{INSTANCE_ID}:{token}``. Returns ``None`` when there is no
  1498	    won claim or the token does not carry our instance prefix (legacy /
  1499	    unfenced path) so callers fall back to strict OP-1062 behaviour.
  1500	    """
  1501	    if claim is None or not claim.ok or not claim.claim_token:
  1502	        return None
  1503	    prefix = f"{INSTANCE_ID}:"
  1504	    if claim.claim_token.startswith(prefix):
  1505	        return claim.claim_token[len(prefix):]
  1506	    return None
  1507	
  1508	
  1509	def _runner_still_owns_claim(
  1510	    client: "jira_dispatch.DispatchClient",
  1511	    key: str,
  1512	    claim: "jira_dispatch.ClaimResult | None",
  1513	) -> bool:
  1514	    """OP-1541: True iff this runner's fencing-token claim is still the live
  1515	    winner on ``key``.
  1516	
  1517	    Gates destructive recovery so ONLY the current winning claim holder may
  1518	    clear assignee / revert (the OP-1541 invariant). Returns ``True`` when we
  1519	    hold no fenced token to disprove ownership (legacy path) or when the live
  1520	    label fetch fails — both fall back to the pre-OP-1541 OP-1062 behaviour
  1521	    rather than silently skipping a legitimate revert on a transient fault.
  1522	    """
  1523	    token = _claim_token_suffix(claim)
  1524	    if token is None:
  1525	        return True
  1526	    try:
  1527	        labels = jira_dispatch.fetch_labels(client, key)
  1528	    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — fail toward the OP-1062 revert
  1529	        print(
  1530	            f"[runner] claim-ownership label fetch failed for {key}: "
  1531	            f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}; assuming still-owner.",
  1532	            file=sys.stderr,
  1533	        )
  1534	        return True
  1535	    return jira_dispatch.is_winning_claim_owner(labels, INSTANCE_ID, token)

     1	"""OP-1106 / v2-Ⅹ-1bc — Runner coordination substrate (shadow-only at land time).
     2	
     3	Backwards-compat: safe (additive module + table; no consumer reads it yet).
     4	
     5	Provides a 4-function API for runner claim coordination backed by the
     6	``runner_claims`` Postgres/SQLite table (alembic 0234). Replaces the
     7	JIRA-label-based mutex (OP-977's ``find_mutex_holders`` +
     8	``claim_ticket_atomic`` in :mod:`backend.agents.jira_dispatch`) over
     9	the next Atlas tickets:
    10	
    11	* :func:`acquire_claim` — atomic INSERT; raises :class:`ClaimBlocked`
    12	  on resource collision. Idempotent for same-owner re-acquire.
    13	* :func:`release_claim` — soft delete (``state='released'``); fencing
    14	  token must match the active row. Idempotent: releasing an
    15	  already-released or never-existed lease is a no-op.
    16	* :func:`record_phase` — heartbeat + phase tracker on active claim.
    17	  Used by long-running tickets to signal liveness.
    18	* :func:`find_active_holders` — read-side query that replaces the JQL
    19	  ``find_mutex_holders`` once OP-1108 cuts the read path over.
    20	
    21	Fencing token format extends OP-977's
    22	``claim:{instance}:{epoch_us}-{uuid}`` so callers can reuse the
    23	existing label-parsing helpers during the strangler-pattern migration.
    24	
    25	Schema reference: see docstring of
    26	``backend/alembic/versions/0234_runner_claims.py`` §"Schema rationale".
    27	
    28	Why sqlite3 (sync) and not asyncpg/aiosqlite
    29	--------------------------------------------
    30	The three runner entry points
    31	(``auto-runner-jira.py`` / ``auto-runner-multi.py`` /
    32	``auto-runner-codex.py``) are sync code paths. Wrapping them in async
    33	just for the claim layer would force every caller to bridge contexts;
    34	the claim path is also short-lived (single INSERT/UPDATE per
    35	transition) so the sync ergonomics win. When the consumer is the
    36	async webhook handler (Sprint H), a thin async adapter can be added
    37	without changing the public API.

   124	def _now_iso() -> str:
   125	    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ")

   128	def _make_fencing_token(instance_id: str) -> str:
   129	    """Per OP-977: ``claim:{instance}:{epoch_us}-{uuid}``."""
   130	    epoch_us = int(datetime.now(timezone.utc).timestamp() * 1_000_000)
   131	    return f"claim:{instance_id}:{epoch_us}-{uuid.uuid4()}"

   134	def _db_path() -> Path:
   135	    """Return SQLite DB path (matches alembic env.py convention)."""
   136	    env_path = os.getenv("OMNISIGHT_DATABASE_PATH")
   137	    if env_path:

   142	@contextmanager
   143	def _conn() -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:
   144	    """Open a sqlite3 connection with explicit transaction control.
   145	
   146	    ``isolation_level=None`` puts the connection in autocommit mode at
   147	    the driver layer; the caller manages BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK
   148	    explicitly via :meth:`sqlite3.Connection.execute`. This is the
   149	    pattern recommended by the sqlite3 stdlib docs for code that needs
   150	    explicit transaction boundaries.
   151	    """
   152	    db_path = _db_path()
   153	    db_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   154	    conn = sqlite3.connect(str(db_path), isolation_level=None, timeout=10.0)
   155	    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
   156	    try:
   157	        yield conn
   158	    finally:
   159	        conn.close()

   166	    except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError):

   169	        lease_id=row["lease_id"],
   170	        ticket_key=row["ticket_key"],
   171	        resource_key=row["resource_key"],
   172	        owner_agent_class=row["owner_agent_class"],
   173	        owner_instance_id=row["owner_instance_id"],
   174	        fencing_token=row["fencing_token"],

   176	        phase=row["phase"],
   177	        heartbeat_at=row["heartbeat_at"],
   178	        acquired_at=row["acquired_at"],
   179	        released_at=row["released_at"],

   181	        external_refs=refs,

   195	    external_refs: Optional[dict] = None,
   196	) -> ClaimLease:
   197	    """Atomically claim ``resource_key`` for ``ticket_key``.
   198	
   199	    Returns the resulting :class:`ClaimLease`. Raises
   200	    :class:`ClaimBlocked` (with ``existing_lease`` populated when
   201	    readable) if a different active lease holds ``resource_key``.
   202	
   203	    **Idempotency**: re-acquiring an existing active claim by the same
   204	    ``(ticket_key, resource_key, owner_agent_class, owner_instance_id)``
   205	    returns the existing lease unchanged — matching the OP-977
   206	    same-bot fast-fail behaviour. Different owner on a held resource
   207	    → :class:`ClaimBlocked`.
   208	    """

   219	                "WHERE resource_key = ? AND state = 'active' LIMIT 1",
   220	                (resource_key,),
   221	            ).fetchone()

   225	                    row["ticket_key"] == ticket_key

   227	                    and row["owner_instance_id"] == owner_instance_id
   228	                ):

   231	                conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
   232	                raise ClaimBlocked(resource_key, _row_to_lease(row))
   233	
   234	            try:

   237	                    "lease_id, ticket_key, resource_key, owner_agent_class, "
   238	                    "owner_instance_id, fencing_token, state, phase, "
   239	                    "heartbeat_at, acquired_at, released_at, release_reason, "
   240	                    "external_refs) VALUES ("
   241	                    "?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 'active', ?, ?, ?, NULL, NULL, ?)",
   242	                    (
   243	                        lease_id,
   244	                        ticket_key,
   245	                        resource_key,
   246	                        owner_agent_class,
   247	                        owner_instance_id,
   248	                        fencing_token,
   249	                        phase,
   250	                        now,
   251	                        now,
   252	                        refs_json,
   253	                    ),
   254	                )

   134	    dag: DAG, *,

   139	    validation_errors: Optional[list[DagValidationError]] = None,
   140	    conn=None,
   141	) -> StoredPlan:
   142	    """Insert a fresh plan row. Use `set_status` for transitions."""
   143	    if status not in _VALID_STATUSES:
   144	        raise ValueError(f"unknown status {status!r}")
   145	    if conn is None:
   146	        async with get_pool().acquire() as owned:
   147	            new_id = await _save_plan_impl(
   148	                owned, dag, run_id, parent_plan_id,
   149	                status, mutation_round, validation_errors,
   150	            )
   151	    else:
   152	        new_id = await _save_plan_impl(
   153	            conn, dag, run_id, parent_plan_id,
   154	            status, mutation_round, validation_errors,
   155	        )
   156	    logger.info(
   157	        "dag plan saved id=%s dag=%s status=%s round=%d",
   158	        new_id, dag.dag_id, status, mutation_round,
   159	    )
   160	    return await get_plan(new_id, conn=conn)

   208	async def _set_status_impl(
   209	    conn, plan_id: int, new_status: str, run_id: Optional[str],
   210	) -> None:
   211	    # SELECT FOR UPDATE holds a row-level lock for the duration of the
   212	    # tx — concurrent set_status on the same plan_id serialise on the
   213	    # lock. Without it, two callers could both read status=validated,
   214	    # both compute "validated → executing is legal", both UPDATE; the
   215	    # double-transition is technically idempotent but produces
   216	    # surprising ordering in timestamps and logs.
   217	    row = await conn.fetchrow(
   218	        "SELECT status FROM dag_plans WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE",
   219	        plan_id,
   220	    )
   221	    if not row:
   222	        raise LookupError(f"no dag_plan id={plan_id}")
   223	    current = row["status"]
   224	    if new_status not in _ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS[current]:
   225	        raise ValueError(
   226	            f"illegal transition {current!r} → {new_status!r} "
   227	            f"(allowed: {sorted(_ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS[current])})"
   228	        )
   229	    now = time.time()
   230	    if run_id is not None:

   538	def step(run: WorkflowRun, idempotency_key: str):
   539	    """Decorator: wrap an async callable so it only runs once per
   540	    (run, key). On second call with the same key, returns the cached
   541	    output without invoking the body.
   542	
   543	    Use distinct keys for genuinely separate work (`fetch_repo`,
   544	    `compile/<sha>`, `push/<branch>`); reuse the same key when you
   545	    want exactly-once semantics across crash-and-resume.
   546	    """
   547	    def decorator(fn: Callable[..., Awaitable[Any]]) -> Callable[..., Awaitable[Any]]:
   548	        async def wrapper(*args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
   549	            cached = await _get_step(run.id, idempotency_key)
   550	            if cached and cached.is_done:
   584	                "is_done": s.is_done, "error": s.error,
   585	                "output": s.output if s.is_done else None,
   586	            }

   291	    to a new workflow_run. Returns the run_id + plan_id + status."""

   304	    # 2. Persist + validate + link via workflow.start.
   305	    from backend import workflow as wf

   308	    metadata.setdefault("user", getattr(_user, "email", "operator"))

   318	        )

   323	    if plan is None:
   324	        # Plan persistence failed inside workflow.start — return best-
   325	        # effort so the caller can retry.
   326	        return JSONResponse(
   327	            status_code=500,
   328	            content={"detail": "plan persistence failed",
   329	                     "run_id": run.id},
   330	        )
   331	
   332	    # 3. If the plan failed validation AND caller opted into mutate,
   333	    #    kick the Orchestrator loop.
   334	    if plan.status == "failed" and req.mutate:
   335	        from backend import dag_planner as dp
   336	        # Before we attempt to mutate, drop any pre-warms that were
   337	        # speculatively launched against the prior draft — the
   338	        # replanned DAG will have different in-degree-0 tasks.
   339	        await _cancel_prewarm(reason="dag_mutated")

   345	            )

   347	            return {

   350	                "status": succ_plan.status if succ_plan else "unknown",
   351	                "mutation_rounds": len(loop.attempts),

   353	                "validation_errors": [],
   354	            }

   356	        # proposal already fired inside run_mutation_loop.
   357	        return JSONResponse(

   359	            content={

   367	            },
   368	        )

   371	    #    status we landed at (validated / executing / failed).

codex
One integration issue is now concrete: the bootstrap smoke endpoint currently treats `validated` or `executing` as green, while `prod_smoke_test.py` expects the workflow run to reach `completed`. That means activating an executor changes the meaning of smoke from “submitted and persisted” to “actually executed,” which is a release behavior change if wired into promotion.

   221	def poll_run(run_id: str) -> dict:
   222	    """Poll workflow run until terminal status or timeout."""
   223	    deadline = time.time() + POLL_TIMEOUT
   224	    while time.time() < deadline:
   225	        run = _get(f"/workflow/runs/{run_id}")
   226	        status = run.get("run", {}).get("status", run.get("status", "unknown"))
   227	        if status in ("completed", "failed", "halted"):
   228	            return run
   229	        print(f"  ... status={status}, waiting {POLL_INTERVAL}s")
   230	        time.sleep(POLL_INTERVAL)
   231	    print(f"  TIMEOUT after {POLL_TIMEOUT}s", file=sys.stderr)
   232	    return {}

   244

   247	        failures.append("no steps recorded")

   251	        if not s.get("is_done"):
   252	            failures.append(f"step {s.get('key','?')} not done")

     1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""[OP-762] Release milestone readiness checker.
     3	
     4	Polls unreleased JIRA fixVersions and emits one structured event per
     5	version:
     6	
     7	* ``milestone_ready`` when every promotion gate is green.
     8	* ``milestone_blocked`` with machine-readable reasons when any gate is red.
     9	* ``LabelInvalid`` when the fixVersion carries the retired unattended
    10	  force-promote label ``release:force-promote`` or a near-miss spelling
    11	  (e.g. ``release:force_promote``) -- rejected, not silently honored.
    12	
    13	The integration layer is deliberately thin. Pure gate evaluation is kept
    14	small enough for tests to exercise without live JIRA, Gerrit, or CI access.

    63	    """Emit an operator-facing warning to stderr (the systemd journal)."""
    64	    print(f"{utc_now_iso()} WARN {message}", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)

    67	def parse_timestamp(raw: object) -> datetime | None:
    68	    if not isinstance(raw, str) or not raw:
    69	        return None
    70	    try:
    71	        return datetime.fromisoformat(raw.replace("Z", "+00:00"))

    76	def emit_event(
    77	    event: str,
    78	    *,
    79	    version: str,
    80	    reasons: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None,
    81	    operator_override: bool = False,
    82	) -> None:
    83	    record: dict[str, Any] = {
    84	        "timestamp": utc_now_iso(),
    85	        "level": "INFO" if event == "milestone_ready" else "WARN",
    86	        "event": event,
    87	        "fixVersion": version,
    88	    }
    89	    if reasons is not None:
    90	        record["reasons"] = reasons
    91	    if operator_override:
    92	        # ADR-0019: flag the abnormal/forced outcome so consumers treat it
    93	        # as green for control flow but as a bypassed gate for audit/display.
    94	        record["operator_override"] = True
    95	    print(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True), flush=True)

    98	@dataclass(frozen=True)
    99	class FixVersion:
   100	    name: str
   101	    released: bool = False
   102	    archived: bool = False
   103	
   104

   394	            continue
   395	        raw_labels = row.get("labels") or []
   396	        if isinstance(raw_labels, list):
   397	            labels.update(str(label) for label in raw_labels if label)
   398	        description = str(row.get("description") or "")
   399	        labels.update(_RELEASE_LABEL_RE.findall(description))
   400	        break
   401	    return labels

   404	def resolve_force_promote(labels: Iterable[str], version: str) -> MilestoneResult | bool:
   405	    """Reject retired force-promote labels.
   406	
   407	    Returns ``False`` when no retired override spelling is present, and a
   408	    ``LabelInvalid`` :class:`MilestoneResult` when ``release:force-promote`` or
   409	    a near-miss spelling (``release:force_promote`` ...) is present -- the
   410	    caller should emit that result verbatim and act on nothing else.
   411	    """
   412	    label_set = set(labels)
   413	    collisions = sorted(
   414	        label
   415	        for label in label_set
   416	        if label == FORCE_PROMOTE_LABEL or _FORCE_PROMOTE_TYPO_RE.match(label)
   417	    )
   418	    if collisions:
   419	        return MilestoneResult(
   420	            version=version,
   421	            event="LabelInvalid",
   422	            reasons=(
   423	                {
   424	                    "gate": "operator_label",
   425	                    "code": "label_format_collision",
   426	                    "labels": collisions,
   427	                    "detail": (
   428	                        f"fixVersion label(s) {collisions} match the retired "
   429	                        "unattended force-promote path; use the audited human "
   430	                        "release-train break-glass command instead"
   431	                    ),
   432	                },
   433	            ),
   434	        )
   435	    return False
   436

   439	    version: str,
   440	    *,
   441	    jira: JiraClient,
   442	    gerrit: GerritClient,
   443	    status_reader: StatusReader,
   444	    now: datetime | None = None,
   445	) -> MilestoneResult:
   446	    now = now or utc_now()
   447	
   448	    # ── RT-22: fail closed on retired unattended force-promote labels ───
   449	    try:
   450	        labels = list(jira.fix_version_labels(version))
   451	    except Exception as exc:  # LabelLookupFailedDuringForce — fail closed
   452	        _warn(
   453	            f"LabelLookupFailedDuringForce: {version}: "
   454	            f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc} — treating as no override, normal gating applies"
   455	        )
   456	    else:
   457	        decision = resolve_force_promote(labels, version)
   458	        if isinstance(decision, MilestoneResult):
   459	            # LabelFormatCollision -> LabelInvalid; do not act on anything else.
   460	            return decision

    13	; processes drained from the same shared queue (O2).  Each one
    14	; registers itself in the Redis ``workers:active`` set with TTL 90s
    15	; and writes a heartbeat every 30s — see backend/worker.py.

    22	;
    23	; Graceful shutdown: systemd sends SIGTERM, the worker stops claiming
    24	; new work, finishes in-flight tasks, releases its dist-locks, and
    25	; deregisters from the active set.  TimeoutStopSec gives it 60s to

docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:18:**Relates**: ADR-0038 (Image pipeline on GitLab — kept; this ADR depends on its tag-driven build), ADR-0002 (GitLab primary / GitHub mirror), ADR-0003 (Gerrit review).
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:24:ADR-0001 adopted full GitFlow (5 long-lived branch types) on 2026-05-04 to handle multi-AI parallelism. In practice (2026-05): `develop` and `main` diverged continuously; `main` rotted **175 commits** behind develop; the operator repeatedly force-aligned `main` and hard-cut releases. The develop→main release-cut machinery (ADR-0016 → ADR-0020) wedged on 2nd+ cuts (AUDIT-26), and its `auto_promote_main` consumer was never activated (AUDIT-26d). Meanwhile the GitLab CI image pipeline (ADR-0038) is **tag-driven and branch-agnostic** (`workflow: $CI_COMMIT_TAG =~ /^v.*/`) and already builds prod images successfully (pipeline #32 = v0.5.0-rc5-hotfix4). Prod has de-facto been running tagged **develop** commits; `main` had no real consumer.
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:34:3. **A release = a promoted IMAGE tag + digest recorded in `release_train`** (NOT a `v*` git tag — see Decision RT-20 below; a git tag would trigger the existing CI `^v` build rule and rebuild a different digest, breaking "validated digest == shipped digest"). Candidate images are built from a chosen develop SHA via pipeline-API (`CANDIDATE_SHA`); promotion retags the validated digest to `vX.Y.Z` in GitLab CR.
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:56:1. **Candidate-artifact circular dependency (the deepest hole).** `scripts/sync_staging_to_develop.sh` stages an image tagged with the raw develop SHA, but the GitLab pipeline only builds on `v*` tags (publishes `${tag}`, `sha-${short}`, `latest`) — it never builds a raw develop-SHA image. So "validate on staging BEFORE cutting the tag" is impossible: the candidate image doesn't exist until a tag exists. **Must pick a candidate-artifact model first**: (a) build immutable images for every accepted develop commit (branch pipeline → `sha-${short}`), or (b) auto-create an `rc`/pre-release tag, stage THAT, then promote to final `v*`, or (c) accept that the final tag exists pre-validation and gate DEPLOY (not the tag). Each has different operator semantics.
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:60:5. **Supply-chain signing inconsistency.** Pipeline signs with `COSIGN_KEY` but audit JSON + docs claim `cosign-keyless-gitlab-oidc`. Either implement OIDC keyless or correct the provenance claims — otherwise "immutable tag = trustworthy artifact" is undermined.
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:61:6. **FE feature-flag is net-new work, not a flip.** Existing `backend/routers/feature_flags.py` is an operator/admin registry (leaks owner/rollout/tenant). Need: a frontend-safe `GET /api/feature-flags/effective` (public booleans only, server-evaluated, fail-closed), an FE provider/hook + SSR bootstrap, and **fix the tier-enum drift** (backend `debug/dogfood/early_access/staged/ga` vs FE `debug/dogfood/preview/release/runtime`).
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:62:7. **Registry/`latest` "green-but-not-deployed" risk.** Staging compose still defaults GHCR `:latest`; prod compose defaults `OMNISIGHT_IMAGE_TAG=latest`. Unset tag → deploys newest regardless of approval. Make staging+prod **fail closed** on unset tag; share one registry/tag/digest contract across CI/staging/prod/health. Also: expose `git_ref`/`git_sha` in `/api/version`; make `frontend_compat` an actual gate or stop documenting it as one.
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:75:**Atomic change groups**: {deploy-prod.sh + check_deploy_ref.sh + allowlist + runbook} · {staging-sync + GitLab publication + staging compose registry/tag defaults} · {Gerrit project.config + auto-promote/release-cut systemd disablement} · {FE effective-flags endpoint + lib/api.ts client + provider/hook + enum alignment} · {ADR supersession + runbook + rollback policy}.
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:82:- Staging + prod pull the same registry namespace + immutable tag/digest scheme; unset tag fails closed.
docs/adr/ADR-0040-single-trunk-release-train.md:90:- **RT-20 (final release identity) = IMAGE-TAG-ONLY.** No `v*` git tag is created (avoids the CI-rebuild hazard with zero fragility — no need to special-case the CI workflow rule). Release identity = promoted GitLab CR image tag `vX.Y.Z` (→ validated digest) + `release_train`/`release_audit` row. Git/human provenance = the audit row (git_sha + digests); optionally a NON-`v*`-matching ref like `released/vX.Y.Z` created post-promote (CI never fires on it). Rationale: prod already runs pinned images not git refs; main is retired; the audit row is the authoritative record; avoids fragile CI tag-exclusion logic.

    42	  #
    43	  # Backend containers used to mount /var/run/docker.sock directly, which
    44	  # meant any RCE in the FastAPI app gave the attacker full daemon
    45	  # control (→ `docker run --privileged -v /:/host` = full host root).
    46	  # This sidecar sits in front of the socket and only forwards a minimal
    47	  # verb allowlist that the legitimate sandbox manager needs.
    48	  #
    49	  # The socket itself is mounted :ro on the proxy — Docker UNIX sockets
    50	  # don't actually enforce :ro (all API calls are "writes" from the FS
    51	  # POV), but the attribute is kept as a policy marker.
    52	  #
    53	  # NO `ports:` — this service is internal-only, reachable only via the
    54	  # compose `default` network as `docker-socket-proxy:2375`.
    55	  #
    56	  # Allowlist rationale:
    57	  #   CONTAINERS=1 — list / inspect / create / remove / start / stop
    58	  #                  (backend/container.py primitives for sandbox mgmt)
    59	  #   EXEC=1       — docker exec inside the sandbox containers
    60	  #   IMAGES=1     — sandbox image inspect + pull
    61	  #   POST=1       — required for any mutating endpoint (create/start/exec)
    62	  # Explicit denies (default but pinned for audit trail):
    63	  #   BUILD / AUTH / COMMIT / CONFIGS / DISTRIBUTION / EVENTS / NETWORKS
    64	  #   / NODES / PLUGINS / SERVICES / SESSION / SWARM / SYSTEM / TASKS
    65	  #   / VOLUMES / INFO — none of these are needed by the app today.
    66	  docker-socket-proxy:

    69	    environment:

    72	      - EXEC=1
    73	      - POST=1
    74	      - BUILD=0

    79	      - EVENTS=0

    82	      - NODES=0
    83	      - PLUGINS=0
    84	      - SERVICES=0

   139	  # acceptable because rolling restart only leaves one replica live at a time

   339	def build_catcs_from_dag(jira_ticket: str, dag: DAG,
   340	                         *, acceptance_criteria: str = "",
   341	                         domain_context: str = "",
   342	                         size: str = "M",
   343	                         forbidden_globs: list[str] | None = None,
   344	                         ) -> list[TaskCard]:
   345	    """Produce one TaskCard per DAG node.
   346	
   347	    ``forbidden_globs`` (optional) is applied wholesale to every card
   348	    — useful when the operator wants the entire intake walled off from
   349	    e.g. ``test_assets/**`` (read-only ground truth per CLAUDE.md L1).
   350	    """
   351	    forbidden = list(forbidden_globs or [])
   352	    cards: list[TaskCard] = []
   353	    for i, task in enumerate(dag.tasks):
   354	        allowed = _derive_allowed_globs(task)
   355	        ac = acceptance_criteria.strip() or task.description
   356	        card = TaskCard.from_dict({
   357	            "jira_ticket": _subtask_key(jira_ticket, i),
   358	            "acceptance_criteria": ac,
   359	            "navigation": {
   360	                "entry_point": task.expected_output if _FILE_PATH_HINT.match(
   361	                    task.expected_output) else f"#{task.task_id}",
   362	                "impact_scope": {
   363	                    "allowed": allowed,
   364	                    "forbidden": forbidden,
   365	                },
   366	            },
   367	            "domain_context": (
   368	                domain_context or f"topology_size={size} task={task.task_id}"
   369	            ),
   370	            "handoff_protocol": [
   371	                f"topology_size:{size}",
   372	                f"Run toolchain: {task.toolchain}",
   373	                "Commit changes and push to Gerrit refs/for/main",
   374	            ],
   375	        })

   385	@dataclass
   386	class ScopeConflict:
   387	    card_a_index: int
   388	    card_b_index: int
   389	    a_task_id: str
   390	    b_task_id: str
   420	                                         for t in dag.tasks}
   421	        for t in dag.tasks:
   422	            for dep in t.depends_on:
   423	                children.setdefault(dep, []).append(t.task_id)
   424	
   425	        def _reachable(start: str, adj: dict[str, list[str]]) -> set[str]:
   426	            seen: set[str] = set()
   427	            stack = list(adj.get(start, []))
   428	            while stack:
   429	                n = stack.pop()
   430	                if n in seen:
   431	                    continue
   432	                seen.add(n)
   433	                stack.extend(adj.get(n, []))
   434	            return seen
   435	
   436	        for t in dag.tasks:
   437	            for d in _reachable(t.task_id, children):
   438	                connected.add((t.task_id, d))
   439	                connected.add((d, t.task_id))
   440	            for a in _reachable(t.task_id, parents):
   441	                connected.add((t.task_id, a))
   442	                connected.add((a, t.task_id))
   443	
   444	    conflicts: list[ScopeConflict] = []
   445	    # We pull the task_id from the DAG by index (cards were built in
   446	    # DAG order by ``build_catcs_from_dag``).
   447	    task_ids = [t.task_id for t in (dag.tasks if dag else [])]
   448	    if not task_ids or len(task_ids) != len(cards):
   449	        task_ids = [c.jira_ticket for c in cards]
   450	
   451	    for i in range(len(cards)):
   452	        a = cards[i]
   453	        ai = task_ids[i]
   454	        for j in range(i + 1, len(cards)):
   455	            b = cards[j]
   456	            bi = task_ids[j]
   457	            if (ai, bi) in connected:
   458	                continue
   459	            overlap = _first_glob_overlap(
   460	                a.navigation.impact_scope.allowed,
   461	                b.navigation.impact_scope.allowed,
   462	            )
   463	            if overlap is None:
   464	                continue
   465	            conflicts.append(ScopeConflict(
   466	                card_a_index=i, card_b_index=j,
   467	                a_task_id=ai, b_task_id=bi,
   468	                overlap=overlap,
   469	            ))
   470	    return conflicts

   474	                        ) -> tuple[str, str] | None:
   475	    for g1 in left:

     1	"""O2 (#265) — Message Queue abstraction layer.
     2	
     3	The orchestrator pushes CATC payloads (O0 / ``backend/catc.py``) here;
     4	stateless workers (O3) pull them, take dist-locks (O1 /
     5	``backend/dist_lock.py``), execute, and ack.  This module hides the
     6	backing technology behind a single ``QueueBackend`` Protocol so the
     7	worker pool, gateway, and tests all see one API.
     8	
     9	Contract:
    10	  * ``push(card, priority=PriorityLevel.P2)`` enqueues a CATC payload as
    11	    a fresh ``QueueMessage`` in state ``Queued``.  The message id is
    12	    minted server-side and returned.
    13	  * ``pull(consumer, count=1, block_ms=0)`` claims up to ``count`` ready
    14	    messages on behalf of a worker.  Each claimed message has a
    15	    *visibility timeout* — if the worker doesn't ``ack`` or ``nack``
    16	    before it elapses, ``sweep_visibility()`` puts the message back on
    17	    the queue (state Queued) so a peer can take it.
    18	  * ``ack(message_id)`` permanently removes the message; it succeeded.
    19	  * ``nack(message_id, reason, stack=None)`` increments
    20	    ``delivery_count``; once it crosses ``MAX_DELIVERIES`` (3) the
    21	    message moves to the DLQ stream with the original CATC plus the
    22	    last failure reason and stack.
    23	  * ``set_state(message_id, state)`` lets the worker / orchestrator
    24	    advance the state machine (``Queued`` → ``Blocked_by_Mutex`` →
    25	    ``Ready`` → ``Claimed`` → ``Running`` → ``Done`` / ``Failed``).
    26	  * ``dlq_list(limit=100)`` / ``dlq_purge(message_id)`` / ``dlq_redrive``
    27	    — operator surface for inspecting and recovering DLQ entries.
    28	
    29	Priority queues:
    30	  * Four classes (``P0`` = incident, ``P1`` = hotfix, ``P2`` = sprint,
    31	    ``P3`` = backlog).  Pull always drains the highest-priority bucket
    32	    first; a P3 caller never starves a P0 sitting in the queue.
    33	
    34	Backend selection:
    35	  * If ``OMNISIGHT_REDIS_URL`` is set + the ``redis`` package imports,
    36	    the Redis Streams backend is used.
    37	  * Otherwise the in-memory backend is used (single-process dev / tests).
    38	  * ``rabbitmq`` / ``sqs`` are reserved names; selecting them raises
    39	    explicitly in the factory until real adapters exist.
    40	  * Both implemented backends share observable semantics; that
    41	    equivalence is the contract the test suite enforces.
    42	"""

    78	class PriorityLevel(str, Enum):
    79	    """Ordered low→high importance: P3 backlog, P0 incident."""
    80	
    81	    P0 = "P0"   # incident / outage — drained first
    82	    P1 = "P1"   # hotfix / customer escalation
    83	    P2 = "P2"   # sprint work (default)
    84	    P3 = "P3"   # backlog / cleanup
    85	
    86	    @property
    87	    def rank(self) -> int:
    88	        """0 = highest priority (P0), 3 = lowest (P3)."""
    89	        return {"P0": 0, "P1": 1, "P2": 2, "P3": 3}[self.value]
    90	
    91	    @classmethod
    92	    def ordered(cls) -> list["PriorityLevel"]:
    93	        return [cls.P0, cls.P1, cls.P2, cls.P3]

    95	
    96	class TaskState(str, Enum):
    97	    """Spec state machine.
    98	
    99	    Edges (allowed transitions):
   100	
   101	      * Queued            -> Blocked_by_Mutex | Ready | Failed
   102	      * Blocked_by_Mutex  -> Ready | Failed
   103	      * Ready             -> Claimed | Failed
   104	      * Claimed           -> Running | Queued (visibility expired) | Failed
   105	      * Running           -> Done | Failed | Queued (visibility expired)
   106	      * Done              -> (terminal — ack required)
   107	      * Failed            -> (terminal — DLQ on Nth failure)
   108	    """
   109	
   110	    Queued = "Queued"
   111	    Blocked_by_Mutex = "Blocked_by_Mutex"
   112	    Ready = "Ready"
   113	    Claimed = "Claimed"
   114	    Running = "Running"
   115	    Done = "Done"
   116	    Failed = "Failed"
   117	
   118	
   119	_ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS: dict[TaskState, set[TaskState]] = {
   120	    TaskState.Queued:           {TaskState.Blocked_by_Mutex, TaskState.Ready,
   121	                                 TaskState.Claimed, TaskState.Failed},
   122	    TaskState.Blocked_by_Mutex: {TaskState.Queued, TaskState.Ready,
   123	                                 TaskState.Failed},
   124	    TaskState.Ready:            {TaskState.Claimed, TaskState.Failed,
   125	                                 TaskState.Queued},
   126	    TaskState.Claimed:          {TaskState.Running, TaskState.Queued,
   127	                                 TaskState.Failed, TaskState.Done},
   128	    TaskState.Running:          {TaskState.Done, TaskState.Failed,
   129	                                 TaskState.Queued},
   130	    TaskState.Done:             set(),
   131	    TaskState.Failed:           set(),
   132	}
   133	
   134	
   135	def _check_transition(old: TaskState, new: TaskState) -> None:
   136	    if old == new:
   137	        return
   138	    if new not in _ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS[old]:
   139	        raise InvalidStateTransition(
   140	            f"illegal queue state transition: {old.value} -> {new.value}"
   141	        )
   142	
   143	
   144	class InvalidStateTransition(ValueError):
   145	    """Raised when ``set_state`` is called with a disallowed edge."""
